# Defects meet boundaries {#sec-defect-boundary}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Learning goals"}
- Describe the doubled theory of a defect: why the reflected copy carries the opposite coproduct, so that the bulk symmetry is $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and why the reflected soliton is the conjugate multiplet.
- Recognize transparent defects and invertible lines as quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type, twisted by the symmetry the line implements, and know what is proved about them and in which setting.
- Know which symmetry a jump defect keeps in the doubled picture: one Borel half untwisted and the other twisted by charge conjugation, on two different module structures of $\mathcal W$, with no coideal combining them.
- Fuse a defect onto a boundary, quantum mechanically and classically, and compare the result with the oscillator boundary of Baseilhac, Delius and George.
- Place defect–boundary fusion among the tensor K-matrices of Appel and Vlaar, and among the boundaries with non-invertible symmetries of Shimamori and Yamaguchi.
:::

The doubling trick of @sec-doubling-trick turns a defect into a boundary. Bajnok and George used it to derive the defect axioms from the boundary axioms [@bajnok_george2006], and @prp-doubling made this precise: the doubled reflection equation is the set of triangle relations, boundary unitarity is defect unitarity, and boundary crossing-unitarity is defect crossing. This chapter asks the question that @sec-boundary-qg asked for boundaries and @sec-defect-qg for defects: which symmetry does the doubled boundary preserve? @sec-qsp placed the boundary coideals of Part VII in the theory of quantum symmetric pairs. Here we do the same for the defects of @sec-defect-qg.

Three answers come out. A transparent defect, and more generally an invertible line, is a quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type, the case in which the quasi-K-matrix of Bao and Wang is Lusztig's quasi-R-matrix [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)]. A jump defect is not. Its doubled boundary keeps the diagonal Borel subalgebra, with the defect space $\mathcal W$ as a dynamical boundary module, as was expected before the test; in addition it keeps the opposite Borel subalgebra twisted by charge conjugation, on a second module structure of $\mathcal W$. The two halves are suggested by the two limits of the transmission matrix as $\theta_d\to\pm\infty$ (@prp-defect-twist-limit): a twist line on each value of the defect charge, and a charge conjugation dressed by a shift of the defect charge. Neither limit has a full twisted diagonal symmetry on $\mathcal W$. Finally, a defect in front of a boundary is a new boundary. For sine-Gordon solitons a type-I defect fused onto a Dirichlet boundary gives exactly the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov reflection matrix, scalar factor included, with the defect rapidity as the second boundary parameter, and classically the fusion dresses the boundary K-matrix by the defect matrix $L_d$. The checks are in `code/defect_doubling.py` (20 checks, about 15 s).

## The doubled theory {#sec-doubled-theory}

**The reflected copy.** In the doubled theory $\Phi(x)=(\vec\phi(x),\vec\psi(-x))$, $x\le0$, a $\vec\psi$-particle of rapidity $\theta$ becomes a particle of the second copy with rapidity $u=-\theta$, and the order of $\vec\psi$-particles is reversed (@sec-doubling-trick). As a representation, the reflected particle at rapidity $u$ is the original multiplet at rapidity $-u$; we write $V'(u)$ for it, so $V'(u)=V(-u)$ as a vector space with the action $\pi_{V(-u)}$. Its two-particle states appear in reversed order, and the symmetry, which acts on $\vec\psi$-particles through $\Delta$ in their original order, acts on the reflected order through $\Delta^{\rm op}$. Correspondingly, the reflected copy scatters with $P\check RP$ at the same rapidity difference (@sec-doubling-trick), and $P\check RP$ intertwines $\Delta^{\rm op}$ because $\check R$ intertwines $\Delta$. The algebra acting on the reflected copy is therefore $U^{\rm cop}$, the same algebra $U=U_q(\hat g)$ with the opposite coproduct.

Physically, $x\to-x$ exchanges left- and right-movers, and with them the non-local charges $Q_j$ and $\bar Q_j$ of @sec-nonlocal-charges, which become $e_j$ and $f_j$. The quantum Chevalley involution $\omega_q$ of (-@eq-omega-map) exchanges $e_j$ and $f_j$ and satisfies $\Delta\circ\omega_q=(\omega_q\otimes\omega_q)\circ\Delta^{\rm op}$, so it is a Hopf algebra isomorphism $U^{\rm cop}\to U$. Through it the reflected copy becomes an ordinary $U$-module, and it is the conjugate multiplet: in the principal gradation $V(1/y)\circ\omega_q=\bar V(y)$ exactly, with $\bar V$ as in @sec-an-diagonal-k. Parity maps solitons to antisolitons.

**The doubled symmetry.** The doubled theory has the bulk symmetry
$$
A=U\otimes U^{\rm cop},\qquad \Delta_A(g\otimes h)=\sum\big(g_{(1)}\otimes h_{(2)}\big)\otimes\big(g_{(2)}\otimes h_{(1)}\big),
$$ {#eq-dbd-coproduct}
in Sweedler's notation $\Delta(g)=\sum g_{(1)}\otimes g_{(2)}$. The first factor acts on the $\vec\phi$-copy and the second on the reflected copy: on $M(\theta)=V(\theta)\oplus V'(\theta)$, the element $g\otimes h$ acts as $\pi(g)\varepsilon(h)$ on $V$ and as $\varepsilon(g)\pi'(h)$ on $V'$, with $\varepsilon$ the counit. The doubled bulk S-matrix, $\check R$ on two $V$-particles, $P\check RP$ on two $V'$-particles and the flip on mixed pairs, commutes with $\Delta_A$: the flip does, because the two factors of $A$ act on different copies. The doubled K-matrix (-@eq-doubled-k) lives on $(V\oplus V')\otimes\mathcal W$ with $\mathcal W$ on the right, so $\mathcal W$ is a boundary module, and a symmetry of the doubled boundary is a left coideal subalgebra $B\subset A$, $\Delta_A(B)\subset A\otimes B$, acting on $\mathcal W$ through some representation $\chi$ and on $M(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$ through $(\sigma\otimes\chi)\Delta_A$, exactly as for the coideals of @sec-coideal.

::: {#prp-reflected-copy}
## The reflected copy
**[Established; numerically checked]** (1) The reflected copy carries the $U^{\rm cop}$-modules $V'(u)=V(-u)$, and its S-matrix $P\check R(x_1/x_2)P$ intertwines $\Delta^{\rm op}$. (2) The doubled bulk S-matrix intertwines $\Delta_A$ of $A=U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and not the coproduct of $U\otimes U$. (3) Through $\omega_q$, $V'(u)$ is the conjugate multiplet $\bar V(u)$, and $P\check R(1/y_2,1/y_1)P=\check R_{\bar V\bar V}(y_1/y_2)$ up to a scalar. (4) The doubled K-matrix (-@eq-doubled-k) is a K-matrix of the doubled theory with boundary module $\mathcal W$; its reflection equation is equivalent to the triangle relations (@prp-doubling).
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) $P\Delta(a)P=\Delta^{\rm op}(a)$. (2) On pairs within one copy this is (1) and its analogue for $\check R$; on mixed pairs the action of $A$ factorizes as $\pi(g)\otimes\pi'(h)$, which the flip intertwines. With $\Delta$ in place of $\Delta^{\rm op}$ on the second factor, the $V'V'$ block would need $P\check RP$ to intertwine $\Delta$. (3) $\omega_q$ is a Hopf isomorphism $U^{\rm cop}\to U$, and $V(1/y)\circ\omega_q$ has $e_j\mapsto yF_j$, $f_j\mapsto E_j/y$, $k_j\mapsto k_j^{-1}$, which is $\bar V(y)$; uniqueness of the intertwiner gives the statement about $\check R$. (4) is @prp-doubling.
:::

We checked (2) and (3) for the sine-Gordon solitons and the $a_2^{(1)}$ vector solitons: the doubled $\check R$ commutes with $\Delta_A$ to $10^{-15}$ and fails by 1.7 with $U\otimes U$; for sine-Gordon $\bar V(y)=CV(y)C$ with $C=\sigma_x$ (`code/defect_doubling.py`). The equivalence (4) is checked in `code/defect_axioms.py`.

## Transparent defects and diagonal symmetric pairs {#sec-diagonal-qsp}

**The diagonal coideal.** The transparent defect has $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb T=\bar{\mathbb T}=1$; its doubled K-matrix exchanges the copies. Its symmetry is the image of the bulk symmetry,
$$
\Delta(U)=\Big\{\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}\ :\ a\in U\Big\}\subset U\otimes U^{\rm cop},\qquad
\Delta_A\big(\Delta(a)\big)=\sum\big(a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(3)}\big)\otimes\Delta\big(a_{(2)}\big),
$$ {#eq-dbd-diagonal}
which is a left coideal subalgebra by coassociativity, with $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ carrying the counit. More generally, for any Hopf algebra automorphism $\psi$ of $U$, such as a torus rescaling $e_j\to t_je_j$, $f_j\to f_j/t_j$ or a diagram automorphism, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a left coideal subalgebra, a **twisted diagonal**. An invertible line implements a symmetry of the bulk: $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb T$ an invertible matrix on $V$ with $\mathbb T\pi(a)\mathbb T^{-1}=\pi(\psi(a))$ for some $\psi$. Its doubled boundary is invariant under $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$. The twist defect $\mathbb T=e^{i\alpha\cdot\mu}$ of @prp-twist-defect gives a torus twist, $t_1=1/t_0=e^{2i\alpha}$ for sine-Gordon, and the charge-conjugation line $\mathbb T=C$ gives the diagram automorphism $\tau$ that exchanges the nodes $0$ and $1$. A particle frozen as a defect, $\mathcal W=V(\theta_d)$ and $\mathbb T=\check R$ (@sec-triangle-relations), is invariant under the untwisted $\Delta(U)$, with $U$ acting on $\mathcal W$ by its representation.

**Quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type.** Bao and Wang call $(U\otimes U,U)$, with $U$ embedded by $\varphi=(\omega\otimes1)\circ\Delta$, the quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)]. Their $\omega$ is our $\omega_q$ and their coproduct is that of Part VI, and their coideals are right coideals, as Kolb's are (@sec-letzter-kolb). The map $\omega_q\otimes{\rm id}:U\otimes U^{\rm cop}\to U\otimes U$ is an algebra isomorphism and a coalgebra anti-isomorphism, since each factor reverses the coproduct, so it maps left coideals to right coideals, and it maps $\Delta(U)$ of (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) onto $\varphi(U)$. This is the analogue of @prp-omega-dictionary. At $q=1$, $\varphi(\mathfrak g)$ is the fixed-point algebra of the involution $(x,y)\mapsto(\omega(y),\omega(x))$ of $\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak g$, of the second kind like all the involutions of @sec-symmetric-pairs. Its Satake diagram is two copies of the Dynkin diagram, all nodes white, with $\tau$ exchanging corresponding nodes (by hand). The physical reading is the one above: a boundary of the doubled theory pairs each charge of the $\vec\phi$-copy with the charge of the opposite chirality of the reflected copy.

::: {#prp-diagonal-coideal}
## Transparent defects and invertible lines are diagonal-type pairs
**[Theorem (1)–(2); Established (3); Numerical (4)]** (1) For every Hopf automorphism $\psi$ of $U$, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a left coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$. (2) The doubled boundary of an invertible line with $\mathbb T\pi(\cdot)\mathbb T^{-1}=\pi\circ\psi$, and in particular of the transparent defect ($\psi={\rm id}$), is invariant under it. (3) $(\omega_q\otimes{\rm id})\Delta(U)$ is the coideal of the quantum symmetric pair of diagonal type, whose quasi-K-matrix is Lusztig's quasi-R-matrix twisted by $\omega\otimes1$ [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)] [@wang2023, Ex. 0.1 and Sec. 2]. (4) Let $X$ be the space spanned by the 21 monomials $g\otimes h$ of degree at most one in the generators of one node of each factor ($g,h\in\{k^{-1},1,k,e,f\}$). For the transparent defect (sine-Gordon solitons, a spin-1 probe, the $a_2$ vector solitons), the twist line and the charge-conjugation line, the largest subspace $S\subset X$ that commutes with the doubled K-matrix and is a left coideal subspace, $\Delta_A(S)\subset A\otimes S$, is exactly $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)\cap X$, spanned by $1$, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(k^{\pm1})$, $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(e)$ and $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(f)$. This is a calculation in $X$, not a maximality statement for coideal subalgebras.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) $\Delta_A\big((1\otimes\psi)\Delta(a)\big)=\sum\big(a_{(1)}\otimes\psi(a_{(3)})\big)\otimes(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(a_{(2)})$, by (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) and because $\psi$ is a coalgebra map. (2) On a one-particle state $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(a)$ acts as $\pi(a)$ on $V$ and as $\pi(\psi(a))$ on $V'$, and the off-diagonal blocks of $K$ are $\mathbb T$ and $\bar{\mathbb T}=\mathbb T^{-1}$; the coideal property carries this to many-particle states, as in @thm-k-reflection. (3) is quoted. (4) is numerical (`code/defect_doubling.py`).
:::

The search in (4) shows why the coideal property matters. In $X$ the commutant of the doubled K-matrix on one-particle states is 17-dimensional: it contains, for example, $e\otimes1+1\otimes e$, which acts identically on the two copies of a single particle but fails on a $V\otimes V'$ pair. Imposing the two-particle doubled reflection leaves 7 or 12 dimensions, depending on the probe, because symmetric combinations of Cartan elements of the two copies cannot be distinguished with two particles. Requiring $\Delta_A(S)\subset A\otimes S$, iterated to a fixed point, removes all of this and leaves the 5-dimensional twisted diagonal, to $10^{-15}$, in every case. The procedure mirrors, in a finite space, a theorem of Appel and Vlaar: a quantum symmetric pair subalgebra is the largest coideal subalgebra contained in the fixed points of a certain automorphism built from the universal K-matrix [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 4.1.3]. The space $X$ is not closed under multiplication, so (4) says nothing about coideal subalgebras, and the corresponding maximality statement for $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ is false. The element $c=k_0k_1$ is central and group-like, and it acts as 1 on the level-zero modules $V(\theta)$. So $c^{\pm1}\otimes1$, adjoined to $\Delta(U)$, gives a larger left coideal subalgebra that leaves the doubled boundary invariant; and $c\otimes1\notin\Delta(U)$, since the counit applied to its second factor gives $c$ and applied to its first factor gives 1, while the two agree on $\Delta(U)$.

**What is proved, and where.** Bao and Wang's remark is stated in the finite-type setting of their paper, with "one checks" for the coideal property [@bao_wang2018b, Sec. 1.2 and Rem. 4.10]. Wang's survey repeats it as an example and states that the quasi-K-matrix of the diagonal type reduces to the quasi-R-matrix [@wang2023, Ex. 0.1 and Sec. 2]. Balagović and Kolb construct the quasi-K-matrix in general and do not discuss the diagonal type [@balagovic_kolb2019]. For affine $\hat g$ the relevant Cartan matrix, that of $\hat g\oplus\hat g$, is decomposable, and Kolb [@kolb2014] and Appel and Vlaar [@appel_vlaar2022] assume an indecomposable one, so their constructions of the coideals and of the universal K-matrices, respectively, do not directly cover the diagonal type of affine algebras. Nothing is lost for the physics: for the diagonal type the role of the universal K-matrix is played by the universal R-matrix, which exists for $U_q(\hat g)$ (@sec-universal-r-affine), and the doubled K-matrix of a particle used as a defect is its evaluation. Kolb and Yakimov's "symmetric pairs for Nichols algebras of diagonal type" [@kolb_yakimov2020] concern Nichols algebras with diagonal braiding, an unrelated use of the word.

In conformal field theory the folded image of the trivial defect is the boundary state of the doubled theory that glues the two copies by the identity, which preserves the diagonal chiral algebra; (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) is its massive, quantum-group counterpart.

## Jump defects in the doubled picture {#sec-jump-coideal}

For a jump defect $\mathcal W$ is infinite dimensional and $\mathbb T$ depends on $\theta-\theta_d$. The following conjecture, and the expectation stated after it, were registered when this part was planned, before the test was run.

::: {#cnj-twisted-diagonal}
## Twisted diagonal symmetry of a jump defect
**[Conjecture; refuted for Hopf twists, exact argument below]** The doubled boundary (-@eq-doubled-k) of a type-I defect is invariant under a twisted diagonal coideal $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, with $\mathcal W$ a module of it.
:::

The expectation stated with it was that the conjecture is false as stated: a type-I$_-$ defect keeps only the Borel subalgebra $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ (@sec-borel), so the full diagonal cannot survive, and the likely truth is that a diagonal Borel subalgebra acts, with $\mathcal W$ a dynamical boundary module. The numerical test below confirmed this and found a second, twisted, Borel symmetry; @prp-diagonal-borel states what is proved.

**The test.** A generator $x$ of $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ acts on $M(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$ through (-@eq-dbd-coproduct). For $x=e_j\otimes1+k_j\otimes\psi(e_j)$ this action is $\pi(e_j)\otimes1+\pi(k_j)\otimes Y$ on $V\otimes\mathcal W$ and $1\otimes Y+\pi'(\psi(e_j))\otimes\kappa$ on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$, with unknown operators $Y=\chi(x)$ and $\kappa=\chi(k_j\otimes\psi(k_j))$ on $\mathcal W$; the generators $f_j$ are analogous. The equation $K(\theta)X(\theta)=X(-\theta)K(\theta)$ is linear and inhomogeneous in the unknowns. We solved it by least squares for three rapidities at once, with $\theta$-independent unknowns of the right weight, on windows $\lvert n\rvert\le N$ with $N=5,7,9$ and equations imposed on $\lvert n\rvert\le N-2$. A torus factor in $\psi$ is absorbed into $\kappa$, so the cases $\psi(e_j)\propto e_j$ ("id") and $\psi(e_j)\propto e_{\tau(j)}$ ("$\tau$") cover all twisted diagonals of $U_q(\widehat{sl}_2)$ built from these automorphisms. These are all the Hopf algebra automorphisms of $U$: by a theorem of Twietmeyer, the Hopf algebra automorphisms of $U_q(\hat g')$ over the field of rational functions in $q$ are the torus rescalings composed with diagram automorphisms [@kolb2014, Thm. 3.2], and we use this for generic $q$. Other algebra automorphisms, such as $\omega_q$, which reverses the coproduct, do not give twisted diagonals. Each unknown is restricted to the one shift of $n$ that charge conservation allows. Nothing is lost by this: $\mathbb L=P\mathbb T$ conserves the total charge, so the equation splits into components according to the shift of the total charge, only one component contains the inhomogeneous term, and the other components of $Y$ and $\kappa$ obey homogeneous equations that cannot cancel it.

::: {#prp-diagonal-borel}
## The two Borel symmetries of a jump defect
**[Theorem (1), (3)–(5), and (2) for type I$_-$; Numerical (2) for type I$_+$]** Let $\mathbb T$ be the sine-Gordon transmission matrix of type I$_\mp$ on the Weyl module $\mathcal W$ of $U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$, (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) and @prp-two-borels.

1. The diagonal Borel subalgebra $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))$ is a left coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and the doubled boundary is invariant under it, with $\mathcal W$ the Weyl module.
2. The opposite Borel subalgebra twisted by charge conjugation, $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\pm))$, is also a symmetry, with a second module structure $\tilde\rho$ on $\mathcal W$. For type I$_-$, in the normalization of (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix), with $a=iy_dq^{-s}/(q^2-1)$ and $b=iy_dq^{s}/(q^2-1)$,

   $$
   \tilde\rho(e_1)\lvert n\rangle=a\,q^{-2n}\lvert n+1\rangle,\quad \tilde\rho(k_1)\lvert n\rangle=q^{-2n-2-s}\lvert n+2\rangle,\quad
   \tilde\rho(e_0)\lvert n\rangle=b\,q^{2n}\lvert n-1\rangle,\quad \tilde\rho(k_0)\lvert n\rangle=q^{2n-2+s}\lvert n-2\rangle .
   $$ {#eq-dbd-second-module}

3. No twisted diagonal $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$, with $\psi$ a Hopf algebra automorphism of $U$, is a symmetry, for any $\theta$-independent action on $\mathcal W$: for type I$_-$ the untwisted $e_j$ and the $\tau$-twisted $f_j$ fail, for type I$_+$ the untwisted $f_j$ and the $\tau$-twisted $e_j$.
4. No coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ containing both Borel symmetries acts on any module $\mathcal W$ compatibly with the doubled K-matrix.
5. These are limits of the matrix part. Write $\mathbb T=\Phi\,\hat{\mathbb T}$, with $\Phi$ the scalar factor ((-@eq-sgd-scalar) for type I$_-$) and $\hat{\mathbb T}$ the matrix part, and set $\hat{\mathbb L}=P\hat{\mathbb T}$. For type I$_-$, as $\theta_d\to+\infty$, $\hat{\mathbb L}$ tends to the direct sum over $n$ of the twist matrices ${\rm diag}(q^{-n},q^{n+s})$ on $V\otimes\mathbb C\lvert n\rangle$, and so does $\mathbb L=P\mathbb T$, since $\Phi\to1$ there (@prp-defect-twist-limit). Each charge sector on its own is the twist line with $t_1=1/t_0=q^{-2n-s}$, whose doubled boundary keeps $(1\otimes t_n)\Delta(U)$. As $\theta_d\to-\infty$, $\hat{\mathbb L}$ divided by $y/y_d$ tends to the charge conjugation dressed by a shift of the defect charge of @prp-defect-twist-limit (3), which is not an invertible line with $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$. Here the scalar matters: $\lvert\Phi\rvert=(1+Y^2)^{-1/2}$ with $Y=y/y_d$, so $\mathbb L$ divided by $y/y_d$ tends to zero, while $\mathbb L/(\Phi Y)$ has that limit and $\lvert\Phi Y\rvert\to1$. For type I$_+$ the two directions are exchanged, and the twist matrices are ${\rm diag}(q^{n},q^{-n-s})$. In neither limit does a twisted diagonal $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ act on all of $\mathcal W$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Every intertwining equation below is linear and homogeneous in $\mathbb T$, so the scalar factor $\Phi$ cancels from it, and we write the equations for the matrix part $\hat{\mathbb L}=P\hat{\mathbb T}$ of (5), on $V\otimes\mathcal W=(v_+\otimes\mathcal W)\oplus(v_-\otimes\mathcal W)$. Let $E_+v_-=v_+$, $E_-v_+=v_-$, so that $\pi_y(e_1)=yE_+$, $\pi_y(f_1)=y^{-1}E_-$, $\pi_y(e_0)=yE_-$ and $\pi_y(f_0)=y^{-1}E_+$. For type I$_-$, $\hat{\mathbb L}=\mathcal D+y\,\mathcal O$ with $\mathcal D={\rm diag}(A,D)$ and $\mathcal O=\big(\begin{smallmatrix}0&B\\C&0\end{smallmatrix}\big)$, where $A\lvert n\rangle=q^{-n}\lvert n\rangle$, $D\lvert n\rangle=q^{n+s}\lvert n\rangle$, $C\lvert n\rangle=-iy_d^{-1}q^{-n}\lvert n+1\rangle$ and $B\lvert n\rangle=-iy_d^{-1}q^{n+s}\lvert n-1\rangle$; these four operators are invertible and independent of $\theta$. For type I$_+$, $\hat{\mathbb L}=\mathcal D_++y^{-1}\mathcal O_+$, with blocks of the same kind. A generator $x$ is a symmetry when $\hat{\mathbb L}(\theta)X_V=X_{V'}\hat{\mathbb L}(\theta)$, where $X_V$ and $X_{V'}$ are its actions on $V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$ and on $V'(-\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$, both at the spectral parameter $y$; the block $\bar{\mathbb T}P$ of $K$ gives the same equation at $-\theta$.

(1) $U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$ is a Hopf subalgebra, so (-@eq-dbd-diagonal) holds within it. On $V\otimes\mathcal W$ the action of $\Delta(b)$ is $(\pi\otimes\rho)\Delta(b)$ and on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$ it is $(\pi'\otimes\rho)\Delta^{\rm op}(b)$, so the block $P\mathbb T$ of $K$ intertwines them exactly when $\mathbb T$ satisfies (-@eq-borel-intertwiner); the block $\bar{\mathbb T}P$ follows by unitarity.

(2) For type I$_-$ let $\tilde\rho(e_j)$ and $\tilde\rho(k_j)$ be the actions on $\mathcal W$ of $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(e_j)=e_j\otimes1+k_j\otimes e_{\tau(j)}$ and of $k_j\otimes k_{\tau(j)}$. Then $X_V=\pi(e_j)\otimes1+\pi(k_j)\otimes\tilde\rho(e_j)$ and $X_{V'}=1\otimes\tilde\rho(e_j)+\pi(e_{\tau(j)})\otimes\tilde\rho(k_j)$. For $j=1$ the coefficient of $y^2$ is $\mathcal O(E_+\otimes1)=(E_-\otimes\tilde\rho(k_1))\mathcal O$, which gives $\tilde\rho(k_1)=CB^{-1}$, the operator in (-@eq-dbd-second-module). The coefficient of $y$ gives $Y_{n+1}-Y_n=-iy_dq^{-2n-2-s}$ for $\tilde\rho(e_1)\lvert n\rangle=Y_n\lvert n+1\rangle$, and $\tilde\rho(k_1)\tilde\rho(e_1)\tilde\rho(k_1)^{-1}=q^2\tilde\rho(e_1)$ sets the free constant in $Y_n$ to zero when $q^4\ne1$. The equation for $e_0$ gives in the same way $\tilde\rho(k_0)=BC^{-1}$ and $Y'_{n+1}-Y'_n=iy_dq^{2n+s}$ for $\tilde\rho(e_0)\lvert n\rangle=Y'_n\lvert n-1\rangle$ (@exr-dbd-mixed-twist). With these operators the equations of $k_1\otimes k_0$ and $k_0\otimes k_1$, $\hat{\mathbb L}\,(\pi(k_j)\otimes\tilde\rho(k_j))=(\pi(k_{\tau(j)})\otimes\tilde\rho(k_j))\,\hat{\mathbb L}$, hold as well. Finally $\tilde\rho(k_0)\tilde\rho(k_1)=1$, $\tilde\rho(k_i)\tilde\rho(e_j)\tilde\rho(k_i)^{-1}=q^{a_{ij}}\tilde\rho(e_j)$, and $\tilde\rho(e_1)\tilde\rho(e_0)=\tilde\rho(e_0)\tilde\rho(e_1)=abq^2$ is central, so the $q$-Serre relations hold as for the Weyl module, and $\tilde\rho$ is a representation of $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$. The equations for products of generators follow, since $(\sigma\otimes\chi)\Delta_A$ is an algebra map. For type I$_+$ the second module was found numerically.

(3) Every Hopf algebra automorphism of $U$ is a torus rescaling, possibly composed with $\tau$ [@kolb2014, Thm. 3.2], and a torus factor $t$ can be kept explicit. For type I$_-$ and $\psi(e_1)=te_1$, $X_V=yE_+\otimes1+\pi(k_1)\otimes Y$ and $X_{V'}=1\otimes Y+tyE_+\otimes\kappa$, with $Y$ and $\kappa$ arbitrary operators on $\mathcal W$. The coefficient of $y^2$ is $\mathcal O(E_+\otimes1)=t\,(E_+\otimes\kappa)\,\mathcal O$. The left side maps $v_-\otimes\lvert n\rangle$ to $v_-\otimes C\lvert n\rangle\ne0$, and the right side has no component along $v_-$, so there is no solution. For $\psi(f_1)=t^{-1}f_0$ the coefficient of $y^{-1}$ in the $f_1$-equation is $\mathcal D(E_-\otimes\kappa)=t^{-1}(E_+\otimes1)\mathcal D$; the left side annihilates $v_-\otimes\lvert n\rangle$, and the right side maps it to $t^{-1}v_+\otimes D\lvert n\rangle$. For type I$_+$ the coefficient of $y^{-2}$ in the untwisted $f_1$-equation and the coefficient of $y$ in the $\tau$-twisted $e_1$-equation fail in the same way, with $B$ and $A$ in the roles of $C$ and $D$.

(4) In $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, $\Delta(k_1)\big(e_1\otimes1+k_1\otimes e_0\big)\Delta(k_1)^{-1}=q^2e_1\otimes1+q^{-2}k_1\otimes e_0$, so for type I$_-$ any subalgebra containing both halves contains $e_1\otimes1$ when $q^4\ne1$. It acts as $\pi(e_1)\otimes1+\pi(k_1)\otimes Z$ on $V\otimes\mathcal W$ and as $1\otimes Z$ on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$, and the coefficient of $y^2$, $\mathcal O(E_+\otimes1)=0$, fails as in (3) (@exr-dbd-e-one). For type I$_+$, conjugation by $\Delta(k_1)$ separates the two terms of $f_1\otimes k_0^{-1}+1\otimes f_0$, of weights $q^{-2}$ and $q^2$, so the subalgebra contains $1\otimes f_0$. It acts as $1\otimes Z$ on $V\otimes\mathcal W$ and as $\pi(k_0^{-1})\otimes Z+\pi(f_0)\otimes1$ on $V'\otimes\mathcal W$, and the coefficient of $y^{-2}$, $(E_+\otimes1)\mathcal O_+=0$, fails.

(5) The off-diagonal blocks of $\hat{\mathbb L}$ are $y/y_d$ times $\theta$-independent operators for type I$_-$, and $y_d/y$ times such operators for type I$_+$ (@prp-two-borels), which gives the limits. On $\mathbb C\lvert n\rangle$, ${\rm diag}(q^{-n},q^{n+s})$ conjugates $\pi(e_1)$ into $q^{-2n-s}\pi(e_1)$ and $\pi(e_0)$ into $q^{2n+s}\pi(e_0)$, so (2) of @prp-diagonal-coideal applies. On all of $\mathcal W$, let $\hat{\mathbb L}=\mathcal D$ and $\psi(e_1)=te_1$. The coefficient of $y$ in the $e_1$-equation forces $\chi(\Delta(k_1))=t^{-1}AD^{-1}$, and the coefficient of $y^{-1}$ in the $f_1$-equation forces $\chi(\Delta(k_1^{-1}))=t^{-1}D^{-1}A$. These are the same operator, $t^{-1}q^{-2n-s}$ on $\lvert n\rangle$, and their product $t^{-2}q^{-4n-2s}$ is not 1 on more than one charge sector. In the off-diagonal limit $\hat{\mathbb L}\propto\mathcal O$, and the $\tau$-twisted equations force $\chi(k_1\otimes k_0)=t^{-1}CB^{-1}$ and $\chi(k_1^{-1}\otimes k_0^{-1})=t^{-1}B^{-1}C$, which both raise $n$ by 2 and so cannot be inverse to each other. The twisted diagonals of the other kind fail in each limit already at the level of single generators, as in (3). Type I$_+$ is the same with the directions exchanged.
:::

The numbers: in (1) the residual is $2\times10^{-15}$ for both types, windows $N=6,8$ and offsets $s=0,0.3$; in (2) and the corresponding tests for type I$_+$, at most $6\times10^{-15}$ on all windows, and the relations and the four generator equations of (2) hold exactly for symbolic $n$. In the least-squares test above the failing generators of (3) leave minimal residuals between 0.93 and 0.97, stable from $N=5$ to $N=9$; their values depend on the sampled rapidities, and (3) itself is exact. The operator $\tilde\rho(k_1)$ commutes with $\rho(k_1)={\rm diag}(q^{2n+s})$ only up to $q^4$, although $k_1\otimes k_1$ and $k_1\otimes k_0$ commute in $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, and $e_1\otimes1$ (type I$_-$) and $1\otimes f_0$ (type I$_+$) fail with residuals 0.96 and 0.97. Near the limits of (5), for $N=6$, the untwisted $e$-generator of type I$_-$ leaves the residuals 0.44, 0.063, 0.008 at $\theta_d=1.5$, 3, 4.5, falling roughly like $e^{-\lambda\theta_d}$, and the $\tau$-twisted $f$-generator leaves 0.27, 0.036, 0.005 at $\theta_d=-1.5,-3,-4.5$. For type I$_+$ the same decay occurs with the directions exchanged, and in the opposite directions the residuals stay at 1.00. Each generator is fitted with its own $\kappa$, so these residuals measure how fast $\mathbb L$ approaches its limit, not the relations of a module (`code/defect_doubling.py`).

**Reading the result.** As $\theta-\theta_d\to-\infty$ the type-I$_-$ defect becomes a superposition of twist lines, one for each value of the defect charge, and as $\theta-\theta_d\to+\infty$ a charge conjugation dressed by a shift of the defect charge (@prp-defect-twist-limit). A single twist line has a full twisted diagonal symmetry, and so does the charge-conjugation line $C$ with $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$. At finite $\theta_d$ the defect keeps one Borel half of each: the half $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ of the twist line's diagonal, and the half $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ of the charge-conjugation line's diagonal. This is the quantum form of the massless defect (-@eq-dq-massless-defect), which passes one chirality and charge-conjugates the other. By (5), the other halves do not return in the limits: the twist $t_n$ depends on the defect charge, so different sectors would need different twisted diagonals, and the shift of the defect charge in the other limit cannot be absorbed into an action on $\mathcal W$. The second module structure has an equally concrete origin. The map $\psi\to-\psi$ takes type I$_-$ to type I$_+$ (@prp-two-borels (3)), and on the doubled theory it acts as charge conjugation on the reflected copy, that is, as $\tau$ on the second factor of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$. The $\tau$-twisted $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ is therefore the $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ symmetry of the same defect read as a type-I$_+$ defect, whose charge is the other combination $-(a+b)$ of Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon's two labels; in the one-label module that combination is not diagonal, and its $q$-power acts as the shift $\tilde\rho(k_1)$. (This is an interpretation; the check is (2).) Part (4) shows that the two Borel halves are genuinely separate: they are symmetries of the same operator, but not the image of one coideal acting on one module. In particular @prp-diagonal-borel corrects nothing in @sec-borel, where it was shown that the $e_j$ do not extend the symmetry with the untwisted coproduct; they survive twisted.

@fig-dbd-symmetries summarizes the two Borel symmetries of the jump defect and the two limits of its transmission matrix.

![Symmetries of the doubled boundary of a sine-Gordon type-I$_-$ jump defect (@prp-diagonal-borel, @tbl-dbd-symmetries). Top: as $\theta_d\to+\infty$ the transmission matrix tends, on each defect charge $n$, to a twist line (@prp-defect-twist-limit), whose doubled boundary keeps the twisted diagonal $(1\otimes t_n)\Delta(U)$; the transparent line is the case $t=1$. As $\theta_d\to-\infty$ it becomes proportional to a charge conjugation dressed by a shift of the defect charge; the charge-conjugation line $C$ itself keeps $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U)$. At finite $\theta_d$ the doubled boundary keeps one Borel half of each (solid boxes): $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$ on the Weyl module $\rho$, and $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$ on the second module $\tilde\rho$ of (-@eq-dbd-second-module). The other halves (dashed) are lost, and they do not return in the limits on all of $\mathcal W$ (@prp-diagonal-borel (5)); no coideal subalgebra containing both kept halves is a symmetry. Bottom: the probability that a soliton is converted, $|\Phi C_n|^2=Y^2/(1+Y^2)$ with $Y=e^{\lambda(\theta-\theta_d)}$, from (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) with the scalar factor (-@eq-sgd-scalar), against $\lambda(\theta_d-\theta)$. The transmission is diagonal, a twist, for $\theta_d\gg\theta$, and off-diagonal, a conjugation, for $\theta_d\ll\theta$. The script checks the conversion probability at $\lambda=1.37$, and that the two limiting blocks act on the soliton multiplet as a torus twist and as $\tau$ (`code/figures/ch43_f41_doubled_symmetries.py`).](figures/ch43_f41_doubled_symmetries.svg){#fig-dbd-symmetries fig-alt="A schematic with three groups of boxes. In the middle, the jump defect keeps two Borel subalgebras, one drawn in blue and one in orange. On the right, the twist lines, one for each defect charge, approached as theta_d goes to plus infinity, have a full diagonal symmetry split into two halves, of which the blue half is the one the defect keeps. On the left, the charge conjugation approached as theta_d goes to minus infinity, with a shift of the defect charge, is compared with the charge-conjugation line, whose twisted diagonal is split into two halves, of which the orange half is kept. The dashed halves do not return in the limits. Below, a curve falls from 1 to 0 as the defect rapidity increases: the probability that a soliton is converted."}

**Beyond sine-Gordon.** For $a_r^{(1)}$ the limits of the type-I$_-$ defect are again twist lines as $\theta_d\to+\infty$, but as $\theta_d\to-\infty$ the defect acts by the rotation $\pi$ of the affine Dynkin diagram (@prp-an-defect-delay), the same $\pi$ that enters $\mathsf D=2(1-\pi)^{-1}$ (-@eq-d-matrix); on solitons the rotation is dressed by a shift of the defect charge, as for $a_1^{(1)}$, where the rotation is the node exchange $\tau$. The natural expectation is therefore that the doubled boundary of an $a_r^{(1)}$ type-I$_-$ defect keeps $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$ and the rotation-twisted $(1\otimes\pi)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$, the latter on a second module structure of $\mathcal W$. @prp-dpt-doubled proves this for type I$_-$ of every $a_r^{(1)}$, $r\ge2$, with the transmission matrices of @sec-soliton-transmission and $\pi(e_j)=e_{j-1}$; the opposite rotation fails. The second module structure is explicit, (-@eq-dpt-second-module), and for $h=2$ it reduces to (-@eq-dbd-second-module).

**The RTT presentation of the off-diagonal doubled boundary.** Write the off-diagonal blocks of (-@eq-doubled-k) in fixed slots, $P\mathbb T(\theta)=\mathbb L(\theta)$ and $\bar{\mathbb T}(\theta)P=\mathbb L(-\theta)^{-1}$ by (-@eq-defect-unitarity). The doubled reflection equation splits into blocks according to the copies of the two incoming particles (@prp-doubling): the block from $VV$ to $V'V'$ is the RTT relation (-@eq-triangle-rtt) for $\mathbb L$, the block from $V'V'$ to $VV$ is the same relation for $\mathbb L^{-1}$, and the mixed blocks are relations of the form $\mathbb L_2^{-1}R_{12}\mathbb L_1=\mathbb L_1R_{12}\mathbb L_2^{-1}$, at the appropriate rapidities, which follow from RTT by multiplication with the inverses. So if the diagonal blocks of the doubled K-matrix are set to zero and boundary unitarity is imposed, which makes the two remaining blocks inverse to each other, the reflection-equation relations become those of the Yang–Baxter algebra of @tbl-boundary-defect-algebra with the inverse matrix adjoined. Setting generators to zero takes a quotient of the reflection-equation algebra of the doubled theory, so this is an equivalence of presentations; no embedding of the Yang–Baxter algebra into the reflection-equation algebra is claimed. The coideals behave in a similar way. A Borel subalgebra is a Hopf subalgebra of $U$, and $\Delta$ maps it isomorphically, as an algebra, onto the left coideal $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))$ of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$; this is why the doubled boundary can carry a module of the same kind as the defect itself. That coideal is not a Hopf subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$, since $\Delta_A(\Delta(e))=(e\otimes1)\otimes1+(k\otimes1)\otimes\Delta(e)+(k\otimes e)\otimes\Delta(k)$ has first factors outside $\Delta(U)$; the Hopf structure it inherits from the Borel subalgebra is not the restriction of $\Delta_A$.

**$\mathcal W$ as a dynamical boundary module.** In the sense of @sec-dynamical-boundary, the doubled boundary of a jump defect is a dynamical boundary: the boundary algebra $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp))\cong U_q(\mathfrak b^\mp)$ acts on the boundary space $\mathcal W$, a $q$-oscillator Weyl module (-@eq-weyl-module), and the K-matrix is its intertwiner. Baseilhac and Koizumi's quantized oscillator boundary of sine-Gordon theory is also a dynamical boundary with an infinite-dimensional boundary module, but of the $q$-Onsager algebra of @sec-q-onsager [@baseilhac_koizumi2003]. The two kinds of boundary are compared classically in @sec-defect-boundary-fusion.

| Line | Defect space $\mathcal W$ | Symmetry of the doubled boundary | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| transparent, $\mathbb T=1$ | $\mathbb C$ | $\Delta(U)$; diagonal type [@bao_wang2018b] | [Theorem]; largest coideal subspace in $X$ [Numerical] |
| twist line $e^{i\alpha\cdot\mu}$ | $\mathbb C$ | $(1\otimes t)\Delta(U)$, $t$ a torus twist | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| charge conjugation $C$ | $\mathbb C$ | $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U)$ | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| particle as defect, $\mathbb T=\check R$ | $V(\theta_d)$ | $\Delta(U)$, $U$ acting on $\mathcal W$ | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| type I$_-$ jump | Weyl module of $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ | $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$ on $\rho$ and $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$ on $\tilde\rho$; no twisted diagonal | [Theorem]; [Numerical] |
| type I$_+$ jump | Weyl module of $U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$ | $\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^+))$ and $(1\otimes\tau)\Delta(U_q(\mathfrak b^-))$; no twisted diagonal | [Theorem]; second module [Numerical] |
| type I$_-$, $\theta_d\to+\infty$ / $-\infty$ | as above | twist line with $(1\otimes t_n)\Delta(U)$ on each charge sector / charge conjugation with a shift of the charge; no twisted diagonal on all of $\mathcal W$ | [Theorem] |

: Symmetries of the doubled boundaries of sine-Gordon lines. $\tau$ exchanges the nodes $0,1$; $t_n$ depends on the defect charge. {#tbl-dbd-symmetries}

## Fusing defects onto boundaries {#sec-defect-boundary-fusion}

**The fused reflection matrix.** Let a defect stand in front of a boundary with reflection matrix $K(\theta):V(\theta)\to V(-\theta)$. A particle crosses the defect, is reflected, and crosses back, so the composite is a boundary with boundary module $\mathcal W$ and reflection matrix
$$
K_{\rm f}(\theta)=\bar{\mathbb T}(\theta)\,\big(1_{\mathcal W}\otimes K(\theta)\big)\,\mathbb T(\theta):\ V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W\to V(-\theta)\otimes\mathcal W ,
$$ {#eq-dbd-fused-k}
with $\mathcal W$ on the right as in @sec-doubling-trick, and $\bar{\mathbb T}(\theta)=\mathbb T(-\theta)^{-1}$. This is Sklyanin's dressing of a K-matrix [@sklyanin1988], Bajnok and George's (19) [@bajnok_george2006] and Corrigan and Zambon's (2.9) [@cz2012], whose $\hat T(\theta)=T(-\theta)^{-1}$ is our $\bar{\mathbb T}$. For scalar factors it is the fusion $K'=\bar{\mathbb T}K\mathbb T$ of @sec-doubling-trick, and for the scaling Lee–Yang model it gives $K_b=\bar{\mathbb T}_bK_{(\mathbb 1)}\mathbb T_b$ (@sec-defect-lee-yang).

::: {#prp-defect-fusion-k}
## Defect–boundary fusion
**[Theorem (1); Numerical (2)–(3); (4) by hand, given the quantum UV–IR matching]** (1) If $K$ satisfies the reflection equation and boundary unitarity, and $\mathbb T$ the triangle relations and defect unitarity, then (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) satisfies the reflection equation (-@eq-reflection-braid) on $V\otimes V\otimes\mathcal W$ and boundary unitarity. (2) **Sinh-Gordon** [@bajnok_simon2008]: $\bar{\mathbb T}_{\rm shG}(\theta)K_D(\theta;E)\mathbb T_{\rm shG}(\theta)=K_{\rm shG}(\theta;E,F=2i\theta_d/\pi)$, with $K_{\rm shG}$ of (-@eq-shg-reflection). (3) **Sine-Gordon solitons.** Let $\mathbb T$ be the type-I$_-$ matrix (-@eq-sg-transmission-matrix) with its scalar factor (-@eq-sgd-scalar), and $K_D$ the Dirichlet reflection matrix, the limit $\vartheta\to\infty$ of (-@eq-bsg-k-full) at $\eta=\eta_D$. Then $K_{\rm f}$ conserves the total topological charge, and on each charge sector $\{v_+\otimes\lvert n\rangle,v_-\otimes\lvert n+1\rangle\}$ it is, after a diagonal change of basis, the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov matrix (-@eq-bsg-k-full) with
$$
\eta=\eta_D,\qquad\vartheta=\lambda\,\theta_d ,
$$
scalar factor included. (4) The classical fusion of @sec-sg-breather-transmission gives a Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov boundary whose parameters agree with (3) in the classical limit of @cnj-bsg-uv-ir. If, beyond that limit, the quantum fused boundary obeys @cnj-bsg-uv-ir with the normal-ordered parameters of the classical fused boundary, then $\lambda\theta_d=(\lambda+1)\theta_d^{\rm cl}$, which is the sine-Gordon form of @cnj-defect-parameter.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) Each side of the reflection equation for $K_{\rm f}$ can be reduced, by the triangle relations, to $\bar{\mathbb T}\bar{\mathbb T}$ times a side of the reflection equation for $K$ times $\mathbb T\mathbb T$, as in Sklyanin's dressing; unitarity follows from $\bar{\mathbb T}(-\theta)\mathbb T(\theta)=1$. (2) $\bar{\mathbb T}_{\rm shG}\mathbb T_{\rm shG}=(\cosh\theta_d+i\sinh\theta)/(\cosh\theta_d-i\sinh\theta)$, which is $1/\big((1-F)(1+F)\big)$ at $\cos\frac{\pi F}2=\cosh\theta_d$ (@exr-sgd-fusion). (3) The block structure follows from the charge conservation of $\mathbb T$ and $K_D$; the identification is numerical. (4) Classically the fused boundary has $C_{0,1}=\cosh(\theta_d^{\rm cl}\pm\frac{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D}2)$, so the classical limit of @cnj-bsg-uv-ir gives $\eta/(\lambda+1)=\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D/2$, which is (-@eq-bsg-dirichlet), and $\vartheta/(\lambda+1)=\theta_d^{\rm cl}$ (@exr-dbd-fusion-gz). With $\vartheta=\lambda\theta_d$ from (3) this says only that $\theta_d/\theta_d^{\rm cl}\to1$ as $\lambda\to\infty$: terms that vanish in the limit, such as a correction of order $\lambda^{-2}$ to $\vartheta/(\lambda+1)$, are invisible. The hypothesis is that $\vartheta/(\lambda+1)=\theta_d^{\rm cl}$ holds at finite coupling, and then $\lambda\theta_d=(\lambda+1)\theta_d^{\rm cl}$.
:::

We checked (3) on windows $N=5,7,9$: the gauge invariants $K_{++}/K_{--}$ and $K_{+-}K_{-+}/(K_{++}K_{--})$ of the sector blocks do not depend on $n$ ($2\times10^{-15}$) and agree with (-@eq-bsg-k-matrix) at $(\eta_D,\lambda\theta_d)$ ($10^{-15}$), while $\vartheta=-\lambda\theta_d$ or $\vartheta=\theta_d$ fail; $K_{\rm f}$ solves the reflection equation on the windows ($10^{-15}$) and a label-dependent perturbation of it does not. With the scalar factors, $\sigma(i\vartheta,u)\to1$ as $\vartheta\to\infty$, so $K_D=R_0(u)\sigma(\eta_D,u)/(2\cos\eta_D)\,{\rm diag}(ye^{i\eta_D}+y^{-1}e^{-i\eta_D},ye^{-i\eta_D}+y^{-1}e^{i\eta_D})$, and the diagonal entries of $K_{\rm f}$ agree with those of (-@eq-bsg-k-full) to $3\times10^{-9}$, the accuracy of our summation of the scalar factor at complex rapidity. After the common factor $R_0(u)\sigma(\eta_D,u)$ cancels, with $u=-i\theta$, this is the scalar identity
$$
\sigma(i\lambda\theta_d,-i\theta)=\frac{1+y_d^{-2}}{1+y^{-2}y_d^{-2}}\,\frac{\Phi(\theta-\theta_d)}{\Phi(-\theta-\theta_d)},
$$
with $\Phi$ the scalar factor of (-@eq-sgd-scalar): the diagonal entry of the matrix part of $K_{\rm f}$ on a charge sector is $(k_++y_d^{-2}k_-)/(1+y^{-2}y_d^{-2})$, with $k_\pm=ye^{\pm i\eta_D}+y^{-1}e^{\mp i\eta_D}$, and $k_++y_d^{-2}k_-=4y_d^{-1}P_0^+$ at $\vartheta=\lambda\theta_d$. The identity is checked numerically, not proved. Item (2) is re-checked to $10^{-16}$, and Corrigan and Zambon's formulas are checked against direct fusion in their own conventions (`code/defect_doubling.py`).

The matrix part of (3) is Corrigan and Zambon's observation that a type-I defect fused onto a Dirichlet boundary gives the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov solution, with a dependence on the boundary charge that a similarity transformation removes [@cz2012, eqs. (2.16)–(2.18)]. The new points are the parameter map, the scalar factor (so no CDD factor appears), and (4): under the same UV–IR hypothesis, the soliton sector gives the same renormalization of the defect rapidity as the sinh-Gordon breathers in @sec-sg-breather-transmission. The infinite dimension of $\mathcal W$ is visible only in the bookkeeping of the topological charge: a type-I defect fused onto a Dirichlet boundary is an ordinary boundary. Corrigan and Zambon found that a type-II defect, by contrast, produces reflection matrices whose dependence on the boundary charge cannot be removed [@cz2012, eq. (2.19)], a conclusion that survives the correction of two misprints in that formula (@sec-defect-boundary-notes), and Bajnok and Simon that a defect fused onto a Neumann boundary multiplies its reflection factor by a boundary CDD factor [@bajnok_simon2008, eqs. (19)–(20)].

**The classical version.** Let the defect at $x=0$ be followed by a boundary for $\vec\psi$ with a field-independent K-matrix $K_\psi(\lambda)$ satisfying (-@eq-boundary-compatibility), and let the region between them shrink to zero (@sec-sg-breather-transmission). The defect matrix relates the auxiliary solutions on the two sides, $\Psi_\phi=L_d\Psi_\psi$ (@sec-defect-lax), so the transport into the $\vec\psi$ region is $L_d(\lambda)^{-1}$ and the double-row transfer matrix (-@eq-double-row) of the composite system has the boundary matrix
$$
K_\phi(\lambda)=\sigma\big(L_d(1/\lambda)^{-1}\big)\,K_\psi(\lambda)\,L_d(\lambda)^{-1},
$$ {#eq-dbd-dressed-k}
which depends on the boundary values $\vec\phi(0)$, $\vec\psi(0)$: a dynamical K-matrix. It is the classical form of (-@eq-dbd-fused-k), with the inverse defect matrices that @prp-defect-transfer found for the defect operator.

::: {#prp-fused-bdg}
## Fused boundaries and the oscillator boundary
**[Theorem, by hand; numerically checked]** (1) On the fused system, (-@eq-dbd-dressed-k) satisfies $\partial_tK_\phi=K_\phi\,a_t(\lambda)+\sigma\big(a_t(1/\lambda)\big)K_\phi$, so ${\rm tr}\big(K_\phi(\lambda)\mathcal T(\lambda)\big)$ is conserved. This holds for every $a_r^{(1)}$ boundary of @tbl-durham, including Neumann, and both defect types (checked for type I$_-$). (2) The sine-Gordon defect potential (-@eq-sg-defect-potential) of type I$_-$ is the oscillator Hamiltonian (-@eq-bsg-oscillator) at the complex values
$$
\hat p=\frac{\beta_{\rm SG}\psi}2-i\theta_d,\qquad\hat q=\frac{\beta_{\rm SG}\psi}2+i\theta_d ,
$$
up to a constant. A defect fused onto the Dirichlet boundary $\psi=\phi_D$ is the static Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov boundary with $C_1=\cos\hat q=\cosh(\theta_d-\frac{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D}2)$ and $C_0=\cos\hat p$: the oscillator frozen at a complex point. (3) A defect fused onto a Neumann boundary is a dynamical boundary with one boundary variable $\psi(t)$, conjugate to $\phi(0)$ through the defect's kinetic term (-@eq-dc-defect-bracket). It is not the boundary of Baseilhac, Delius and George: there $(\hat p,\hat q)$ is an independent canonical pair, the boundary condition has no $\partial_t\psi$ term, and the oscillator flow does not preserve $\hat p-\hat q=-2i\theta_d$.
:::

::: {.proof}
(1) From $\partial_tL_d=L_d\,a_t(\psi)-a_t(\phi)\,L_d$ (@sec-defect-lax), $\partial_t(L_d^{-1})=L_d^{-1}a_t(\phi)-a_t(\psi)L_d^{-1}$ and the same with $\sigma$ applied at $1/\lambda$. Hence $\partial_tK_\phi-K_\phi a_t(\phi;\lambda)-\sigma(a_t(\phi;1/\lambda))K_\phi=\sigma(L_d(1/\lambda)^{-1})\big[-K_\psi a_t(\psi;\lambda)-\sigma(a_t(\psi;1/\lambda))K_\psi\big]L_d(\lambda)^{-1}$, which vanishes by (-@eq-boundary-compatibility) for $\vec\psi$, since in the limit $\partial_x\vec\psi(0)$ obeys both the defect condition and the boundary condition. (2) Expand the cosines: $\sigma\cos\frac{\beta(\phi+\psi)}2+\sigma^{-1}\cos\frac{\beta(\phi-\psi)}2=e^{i\beta\phi/2}\cos(\frac{\beta\psi}2+i\theta_d)+e^{-i\beta\phi/2}\cos(\frac{\beta\psi}2-i\theta_d)$ with $\sigma=e^{-\theta_d}$ and $\beta=\beta_{\rm SG}$. (3) With Neumann conditions the defect conditions (-@eq-sg-defect-conditions) become $\partial_x\phi=\partial_t\psi-\partial_\phi\mathcal B_d$ and $\partial_t\phi=-\partial_\psi\mathcal B_d$ at $x=0$ [@bajnok_simon2008, eq. (5)], while the oscillator boundary has $\partial_x\phi=-\partial_\phi H_{\rm osc}$ and $\frac{d}{dt}(\hat p-\hat q)=-\frac{m_0}2\big(e^{i\beta\phi/2}\sin\hat q+e^{-i\beta\phi/2}\sin\hat p\big)\ne0$ on the line.
:::

Item (1) was checked with finite differences, at random field values on the fused system, for $a_1^{(1)}$ with a Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov boundary and with Neumann, $a_2^{(1)}$ with $C=(1,-1,1)$ and with Neumann, and $a_3^{(1)}$ with $C=(1,-1,1,-1)$ ($10^{-9}$); with $L_d$ in place of $L_d^{-1}$, or with $K_\psi$ undressed, it fails at order one. Items (2) and (3) were checked with sympy (`code/defect_doubling.py`). Item (1) gives, for $a_n^{(1)}$ with $n\ge2$, dynamical boundaries with $n$ boundary variables and a conserved generating function: a type-I defect fused onto a boundary of @tbl-durham. Part VII's problem 9 (@sec-boundary-open-problems) asked for such boundaries; whether the conserved quantities are in involution, and what the quantum versions are, we have not examined.

The oscillator boundary and the fused boundary are thus related but not equal. Both have the same boundary potential, but in the fused system one combination of the oscillator variables is frozen at $-2i\theta_d$ and the other is tied to the bulk field by the defect's symplectic structure. In the quantum theory the difference is equally clear: fused onto Dirichlet, the $q$-oscillator space $\mathcal W$ of the defect decouples (@prp-defect-fusion-k (3)), while in Baseilhac and Koizumi's quantized oscillator boundary the boundary module is an infinite-dimensional representation of the $q$-Onsager algebra [@baseilhac_koizumi2003].

## Tensor K-matrices {#sec-tensor-k}

Appel and Vlaar turned the fusion formula into a universal statement [@appel_vlaar2024]. For a quantum symmetric pair $U_q(\mathfrak k)\subset U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of Kac–Moody type, with their universal K-matrix $\mathcal K$ and twist automorphism $\psi$ (@sec-universal-k), they define the **tensor K-matrix**
$$
\mathbb K=\mathcal R^\psi_{21}\,(1\otimes\mathcal K)\,\mathcal R ,
$$
and prove that it lies in a completion of $U_q(\mathfrak k)\otimes U_q(\mathfrak g)$, satisfies a twisted intertwining identity, coproduct identities, and a generalized reflection equation on triple tensor products [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 5.6.1, eqs. (5.5)–(5.8)]. So $\mathbb K$ acts on $M\otimes V$ with $M$ only a $U_q(\mathfrak k)$-module, from a category $\mathcal W_\theta$ they introduce, and $V$ a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module. For quantum affine algebras the action on $M\otimes V(z)$, $V$ finite dimensional, is a formal Laurent series [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 6.4.2]. When $M$ is the restriction of an irreducible finite-dimensional $U_q(\hat g)$-module and $V$ is irreducible, it is a scalar multiple of the **trigonometric tensor K-matrix** $R^{\rm norm}_{V^\psi M}(z)_{21}\,(1\otimes K^{\rm trig}_V(z))\,R^{\rm norm}_{MV}(z)$, which satisfies the generalized spectral reflection equation [@appel_vlaar2024, Thm. 6.5.2]. For the $q$-Onsager algebra every finite-dimensional irreducible module is such a restriction, by a theorem of Ito and Terwilliger quoted in [@appel_vlaar2024, Rem. 6.5.3(a)]; in general the conclusion holds whenever the relevant space of intertwiners is one-dimensional [@appel_vlaar2024, Rem. 6.5.3(b)].

In physical terms, $\mathbb K$ is the reflection matrix of a particle $V$ on a boundary carrying the boundary module $M$, and its factorization is (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) with $M$ a particle used as a defect: $\mathcal R$ lets the particle cross $M$, $\mathcal K$ reflects it at the bare boundary, and $\mathcal R^\psi_{21}$ brings it back. Appel and Vlaar's coideals are right coideals and their boundary module stands on the left; ours stand on the right, and $\omega_q$ translates as in @sec-letzter-kolb. Sklyanin used the same dressing to build reflection matrices on larger spaces [@sklyanin1988]. We checked the simplest case: for the sine-Gordon coideal with generic $\hat\epsilon$ and $\mathcal W=V(\theta_d)$, $\bar{\mathbb T}(1\otimes K)\mathbb T$ with $\mathbb T=\check R$ intertwines the coideal on $V(\theta)\otimes\mathcal W$, the space of such intertwiners is one-dimensional, and the reflection equation holds ($10^{-15}$, `code/defect_doubling.py`). By Remark 6.5.3(b) this matrix is therefore proportional to the trigonometric tensor K-matrix; the scalar normalization is not fixed by this argument.

For a jump defect $\mathcal W$ is a module of a Borel subalgebra. Appel and Vlaar's general theorem does not need the boundary module to extend to $U_q(\hat g)$: any module of the coideal subalgebra $U_q(\mathfrak k)$ in their category $\mathcal W_\theta$ will do, and the restriction hypothesis enters only Theorem 6.5.2. What is missing for a jump defect is such a module: a Borel-module structure on $\mathcal W$ does not by itself give an action of $U_q(\mathfrak k)$ compatible with the fused boundary, and none has been constructed here. Two remarks connect (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) with their work. First, by @prp-defect-fusion-k (3) the result is, sector by sector, an ordinary trigonometric K-matrix with shifted parameters. Second, Appel and Vlaar note that in quasi-split type $\mathbb K$ lies in a completion of $U_q(\mathfrak k)\otimes U_q(\mathfrak b^+)$, and propose evaluating the second leg on infinite-dimensional Borel modules to obtain Baxter-type relations for boundaries [@appel_vlaar2024, Sec. 1.6.2], the boundary counterpart of the Q-operators of @sec-q-operators. Defects in front of boundaries are a natural physical setting for that programme.

## Boundaries and non-invertible symmetries {#sec-noninvertible-boundaries}

**Lines fused onto boundaries.** A topological line placed next to a boundary can be moved onto it, and the result is again a boundary. In rational conformal field theory, fusing a Verlinde line onto a Cardy boundary decomposes by the fusion coefficients; the Lee–Yang defect $\Phi$ fused onto the boundary $\mathbb 1$ gives the boundary $\Phi$ (@sec-defect-lee-yang), and Runkel showed that perturbed $(1,s)$ defects fused onto the Cardy boundary $(1,1)$ give the perturbed $(1,s)$ boundaries [@runkel2010] (@sec-perturbed-defects). In the massive theory the fused reflection matrix is (-@eq-dbd-fused-k). For an invertible line, $\mathcal W=\mathbb C$ and $\mathbb T=g$, it is $g^{-1}Kg$: the boundary transformed by the symmetry, which is invariant exactly when $K$ intertwines $g$.

**Lines ending on boundaries.** A line can also end on a boundary, at a topological junction in ${\rm Hom}(L\otimes B,B)$. Shimamori and Yamaguchi call a boundary $B$ weakly symmetric under a fusion category of lines if this space is non-zero for every line $L_a$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, after eq. (1.3)]. Every line can then be pushed onto the boundary, and the boundary amplitudes obey Ward–Takahashi identities. An example is the sum of all Cardy states, $\sum_c\lvert L_c\rangle$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, footnote 13].

**Modified boundary crossing.** Shimamori and Yamaguchi studied the kinks of the minimal models $\mathcal M_p$ perturbed by $\phi_{1,3}$, $p\ge4$, whose $p-1$ vacua carry the fusion action of the non-invertible symmetry $A_p$ (@sec-topological-lines). A kink $K_{ab}(\theta)$, with $a$ the outer vacuum, reflects into $K_{ac}(-\theta)$ with amplitude $R^a_{bc}(\theta)$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (3.1)]. The amplitudes obey boundary unitarity and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation in the usual form, and, when the symmetry is spontaneously broken and $B$ is weakly symmetric, the modified crossing relation
$$
R^b_{ca}\Big(\frac{i\pi}2-\theta\Big)=\sum_d\sqrt{\frac{d_d}{d_b}}\;S^{ba}_{cd}(2\theta)\,R^d_{ca}\Big(\frac{i\pi}2+\theta\Big)
$$ {#eq-dbd-sy-crossing}
[@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (3.29)–(3.32)], with $d_a=\sin\frac{a\pi}p/\sin\frac\pi p$ and $S$ the bulk kink S-matrix in the normalization of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu. Without the factor $\sqrt{d_d/d_b}$ this is Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov's boundary crossing-unitarity. The factor comes from the normalization of the kink states: the boundary contributes a constant $C^B_{ab}=1/(d_bF^B_b)$ that does not depend on the outer vacuum and cancels, so only the bulk factor of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu survives [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (3.22)–(3.28)].

**Consequences.** The Ward–Takahashi identities of the lines reduce to those of $L_2$ [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (4.2)–(4.3)]. For $p\ge5$ they forbid all non-diagonal reflections and make all diagonal ones equal, without using integrability [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (4.12)]. For $p=4$, the tricritical Ising model, the boundary Yang–Baxter equation and crossing leave two scenarios [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eqs. (4.26)–(4.27)]. In the first all reflections are diagonal. In the second the kinks with outer vacuum 2 are reflected off-diagonally, from $K_{23}$ into $K_{21}$ and back, while those with outer vacuum 1 or 3 are still reflected diagonally, with a nonzero amplitude. Both scenarios share the minimal solution of crossing and unitarity [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (4.29)], and for $p\ge5$ the minimal solution is [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (4.35)]; both are ratios of Gamma-function products of the Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov type.

**Relation to @sec-topological-lines.** In the bulk, the modified crossing rule of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu is equivalent to ordinary crossing after a rapidity-dependent renormalization of the kink states, $(d_x/d_y)^{i\theta/2\pi}$ for a kink from $x$ to $y$ (@exr-modified-crossing); Shimamori and Yamaguchi record the corresponding bulk factor [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (2.32)]. The same renormalization works at the boundary. With $\hat R^a_{bc}(\theta)=(d_bd_c/d_a^2)^{i\theta/2\pi}R^a_{bc}(\theta)$ and the conventionally normalized bulk S-matrix, (-@eq-dbd-sy-crossing) becomes Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov's crossing relation: the $\theta$-dependent factors cancel against those of the bulk S-matrix at $2\theta$, and the shifts by $\frac{i\pi}2$ produce exactly $\sqrt{d_d/d_b}$ (@exr-dbd-boundary-crossing, by hand). Unitarity and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation are unchanged by the renormalization. So, as in the bulk, crossing alone cannot tell the two normalizations apart; the Ward–Takahashi identities can, because the action of the lines on kink states is not invariant under rapidity-dependent rescalings.

**Relation to the defects of this part.** The integrable defects of Part VIII are topological lines that are not symmetries: they act on particles through rapidity-dependent transmission matrices, and the invertible lines appear only in their limits (@prp-defect-twist-limit). In the doubled theory a topological line becomes a boundary, and this chapter has identified the boundary symmetries: a twisted diagonal for an invertible line, two Borel halves for a jump defect. For the non-invertible lines of Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu and of Shimamori and Yamaguchi, which act on vacua rather than on the particles' internal labels, the corresponding doubled boundaries and their symmetry algebras have not been worked out.

## Exercises {#sec-defect-boundary-exercises}

::: {#exr-dbd-cop}
Show that $P\check R(x_1/x_2)P$ intertwines $\Delta^{\rm op}$, and that the doubled bulk S-matrix of @sec-doubling-trick commutes with (-@eq-dbd-coproduct). Show that $\Delta_A$ is coassociative. Why does the same S-matrix not commute with the coproduct of $U\otimes U$? Show that $\omega_q$ is a Hopf algebra isomorphism $U^{\rm cop}\to U$ and that $V(1/y)\circ\omega_q=\bar V(y)$ for the $a_n$ vector representation.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-diagonal-coideal}
Prove (-@eq-dbd-diagonal), and deduce that $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$ is a left coideal subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ for every Hopf automorphism $\psi$. Show that $\omega_q\otimes{\rm id}:U\otimes U^{\rm cop}\to U\otimes U$ reverses the coproduct and maps $\Delta(U)$ onto Bao and Wang's right coideal $(\omega\otimes1)\Delta(U)$. Is $\Delta(U)$ a coideal of $U\otimes U$?
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-invertible}
For sine-Gordon solitons, find the automorphism $\psi$ implemented by the twist line $\mathbb T={\rm diag}(e^{i\alpha},e^{-i\alpha})$ and by the charge-conjugation line $\mathbb T=\sigma_x$, and show that their doubled boundaries are invariant under $(1\otimes\psi)\Delta(U)$. What happens to the spectral parameter if $t_0t_1\ne1$?
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-mixed-twist}
For the type-I$_-$ matrix with $A_n=q^{-n}$, $D_n=q^{n+s}$, $C_n=-i(y/y_d)q^{-n}$, $B_n=-i(y/y_d)q^{n+s}$, write out the equation $\mathbb T\big(\pi(e_1)\otimes1+\pi(k_1)\otimes Y\big)=\big(Y\otimes1+\kappa\otimes\pi(e_0)\big)\mathbb T$ on $v_\pm\otimes\lvert n\rangle$, with $Y\lvert n\rangle=Y_n\lvert n+1\rangle$ and $\kappa\lvert n\rangle=\kappa_n\lvert n+2\rangle$. Show that $Y_{n+1}-Y_n=-iy_dq^{-2n-2-s}$ and $\kappa_n=q^{-2n-2-s}$, independently of $y$. Derive (-@eq-dbd-second-module), verify its relations, and show that $\rho(k_1)\tilde\rho(k_1)=q^4\tilde\rho(k_1)\rho(k_1)$.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-e-one}
Show that a subalgebra of $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ that contains $k_1\otimes k_1$ and $e_1\otimes1+k_1\otimes e_0$ contains $e_1\otimes1$ if $q^4\ne1$. Show that the doubled boundary of the type-I$_-$ defect is not invariant under $e_1\otimes1$ for any action $Z$ on $\mathcal W$. *Hint:* compare the terms of order $y^2$.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-fusion-gz}
Compute the charge-sector blocks of (-@eq-dbd-fused-k) for the type-I$_-$ matrix and $K_D={\rm diag}(ye^{i\eta}+y^{-1}e^{-i\eta},ye^{-i\eta}+y^{-1}e^{i\eta})$, and compare with Corrigan and Zambon's (2.18). Show that the blocks are (-@eq-bsg-k-matrix) with $\hat\epsilon_{1,0}=-\cos(\eta_D\mp i\lambda\theta_d)/\sin\pi\lambda$ after a diagonal change of basis. Check that the classical fused boundary, with $C_{0,1}=\cosh(\theta_d^{\rm cl}\pm\frac{i\beta_{\rm SG}\phi_D}2)$, agrees with these parameters in the classical limit of @cnj-bsg-uv-ir. Then assume that @cnj-bsg-uv-ir holds for the fused boundary at finite coupling, with $\vartheta/(\lambda+1)=\theta_d^{\rm cl}$, derive $\lambda\theta_d=(\lambda+1)\theta_d^{\rm cl}$, and compare with @cnj-defect-parameter. Why can the classical limit alone not fix this relation?
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-classical-dressing}
Prove @prp-fused-bdg (1). Why does $L_d^{-1}$, not $L_d$, appear in (-@eq-dbd-dressed-k)? For $a_2^{(1)}$ with a Neumann boundary for $\vec\psi$, write the boundary conditions of the fused system and identify the boundary variables.
:::

::: {#exr-dbd-boundary-crossing}
Let $\tilde S^{ab}_{dc}(\theta)=(d_ad_c/d_bd_d)^{i\theta/2\pi}S^{ab}_{dc}(\theta)$ be the conventionally normalized kink S-matrix [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025, eq. (2.32)] and $\hat R^a_{bc}(\theta)=(d_bd_c/d_a^2)^{i\theta/2\pi}R^a_{bc}(\theta)$. Show that (-@eq-dbd-sy-crossing) is equivalent to $\hat R^b_{ca}(\frac{i\pi}2-\theta)=\sum_d\tilde S^{ba}_{cd}(2\theta)\hat R^d_{ca}(\frac{i\pi}2+\theta)$, and that boundary unitarity and the boundary Yang–Baxter equation take the same form for $R$ and $\hat R$.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-defect-boundary-notes}

Bajnok and George introduced the doubling trick and the fusion of a defect onto a boundary [-@bajnok_george2006]; Bajnok and Simon used fusion to solve the sinh-Gordon and Lee–Yang defects and found the classical fusion onto Dirichlet and Neumann boundaries [-@bajnok_simon2008]; Corrigan and Zambon fused type-I and type-II defects onto sine-Gordon boundaries with reflection matrices that keep track of the boundary charge, and related the result to Habibullin's construction of the general boundary condition from two Bäcklund transformations [-@cz2012]. Dynamical boundaries are due to Baseilhac, Delius and George [-@bdg2002], with the quantum version and the $q$-Onsager algebra due to Baseilhac and Koizumi [-@baseilhac_koizumi2003; -@baseilhac_koizumi2005]. Quantum symmetric pairs of diagonal type, with the quasi-R-matrix as their intertwiner, are discussed by Bao and Wang [-@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)] and in Wang's survey [-@wang2023]; the quasi-K-matrix was introduced by Bao and Wang in their quantum symmetric pair approach to Kazhdan–Lusztig theory of type B [-@bao_wang2018], and Balagović and Kolb constructed it in general, together with the universal K-matrix in finite type [-@balagovic_kolb2019]; Kolb constructed the quantum symmetric pairs of Kac–Moody type [-@kolb2014], and Appel and Vlaar their universal K-matrices [-@appel_vlaar2022]. Tensor K-matrices are due to Appel and Vlaar [-@appel_vlaar2024], building on Sklyanin's dressing [-@sklyanin1988] and on Kolb's braided module categories. Modified crossing for non-invertible symmetries is due to Copetti, Córdova and Komatsu [-@cck2024; -@cck2025], and its boundary version to Shimamori and Yamaguchi [-@shimamori_yamaguchi2025]. The coideal $U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ description of the doubled theory, @prp-reflected-copy (3), @prp-diagonal-coideal (4), @prp-diagonal-borel, the outcome of @cnj-twisted-diagonal, the parameter map and scalar identity of @prp-defect-fusion-k (3)–(4), @prp-fused-bdg, and the renormalization of @exr-dbd-boundary-crossing are stated here.

Corrections and clarifications to the sources made in this chapter:

- **Diagonal type.** Bao and Wang's remark [@bao_wang2018b, Rem. 4.10(2)] is made in the finite-type setting of their paper, with "one checks" for the coideal property. Kolb [@kolb2014] and Appel and Vlaar [@appel_vlaar2022] assume an indecomposable Cartan matrix, so their constructions of the coideals and of the universal K-matrices, respectively, do not directly cover the diagonal type of affine algebras, whose Cartan matrix is that of $\hat g\oplus\hat g$. Their right coideal $(\omega\otimes1)\Delta(U)$ corresponds to the left coideal $\Delta(U)\subset U\otimes U^{\rm cop}$ of the doubled theory through $\omega_q\otimes{\rm id}$. The phrase "of diagonal type" in Kolb and Yakimov [@kolb_yakimov2020] refers to Nichols algebras with diagonal braiding and is unrelated.
- **Corrigan and Zambon (2.18)** [@cz2012]. The fused type-I reflection matrix, which they call equivalent to the full Ghoshal–Zamolodchikov solution, is in book conventions (-@eq-bsg-k-full) with $(\eta,\vartheta)=(\eta_D,\lambda\theta_d)$, and the equality extends to the scalar factors: no CDD factor appears. Their $\hat T(\theta)=T(-\theta)^{-1}$ is the book's $\bar{\mathbb T}$.
- **Corrigan and Zambon (2.19)** [@cz2012]. Their general formula (2.17) agrees with the direct fusion (2.9) of their transmission matrix (2.14) with the Dirichlet matrix (2.16). Substituting their type-II parameters into (2.17) gives, with their $Q^2=q^{-1}$, $h=-(\lvert b_-\rvert^2+\lvert b_+\rvert^2)Q^{-2}$, where (2.19) prints $h=-(\lvert b_-\rvert^2Q^{-2}+\lvert b_+\rvert^2)Q^{-2}$, and it gives every term of $s_-$ with the opposite sign. With both corrections (2.19) agrees with the direct fusion entry by entry, up to a factor common to all entries; with either one alone it does not. The conclusion that no similarity transformation removes the dependence on the boundary charge is unaffected (`code/defect_doubling.py`).
- **Shimamori and Yamaguchi** [@shimamori_yamaguchi2025]. Their modified boundary crossing (3.29) is equivalent to the conventional crossing of Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov for amplitudes renormalized by the same rapidity-dependent kink factors that relate the two normalizations of the bulk S-matrix (their (2.32)); what distinguishes the normalizations is the Ward–Takahashi identities, not crossing (@exr-dbd-boundary-crossing, by hand).
- **Book-internal: the pre-registered @cnj-twisted-diagonal** is refuted for all twisted diagonals built from Hopf algebra automorphisms, by an exact argument (@prp-diagonal-borel (3)), and the expected diagonal Borel symmetry is confirmed. In addition, the opposite Borel subalgebra survives twisted by charge conjugation, on a second module structure of $\mathcal W$ (@prp-diagonal-borel). This refines, without contradicting, the statement of @sec-perturbed-defects that no action of the $e_j$ on $\mathcal W$ extends the $U_q(\mathfrak b^-)$ symmetry with the untwisted coproduct.
